reading_candidates: Opening count of eight independent theorems is unsupported; Chapters 38–44 establish dependent complementary inputs.
Original supplied archive remains unlocated; remove unverifiable section numbers, correspondence table numbering and comparative novelty claims.
Chapter 36 now proves the published necessity theorem; update every quoted-not-proved and sole-unproved-input claim.
The assembly uses existing closure and comparison interfaces as well as the named six hard-input groups; do not claim exactly those groups and nothing else.
Published converse is separate from sufficiency, but this is not evidence that the supplied source says nothing about it or does not reprove it.
Correct plural grammar in the discussion of the two passages.
Failure of known resolution in positive characteristic is not a theorem that a normal variety cannot admit a smooth birational model.
No order permutation or alternate proof is ruled out by this chosen dependency graph.
Carrier input requires nonempty psh source space as well as EP; specify the nonempty-family context instead of treating vacuous EP as enough.
Only the earlier inputs are prohibited from depending on final EP; a source EP hypothesis can be used legitimately after established.
Radiciality from point bijectivity is scoped to finite maps of varieties over algebraically closed k, not arbitrary schemes.
Step 2 is not the only hard imported theorem; reflection includes substantial algebraic descent.
Finiteness at the trivial valuation is the nontriviality witness; pointwise finite width is not a uniform absolute sandwich over all valuations.
The earlier proof chain uses GF finiteness at linear-growth valuations, local ideal arithmetic and other finite normalizations; narrow the exhaustive finiteness claim.
The smooth ideal approximants need the actual nonzero ideal on the chosen big-class construction; say generic point, not generic fibre.
Density and upper semicontinuity alone do not define a unique extension of a divisorial trace; comparison requires psh membership.
Pole-bearing functions are allowed and used, but not all functions produced by FS approximation have poles.
Closure package also includes constants, maxima, sums and scaling; it is not exclusively a decreasing-limit package.
Join construction applies only to nonempty constant-bounded families, not all suprema one could want.
The raw supremum and regularization always exist as functions; what is unavailable before EP is their general psh membership.
The family indexed by real a is independent of the cardinality of k; remove irrelevant uncountable-field assumption.
Index continuous majorants by reverse pointwise order to make the decreasing net precise.

Ample perturbations do not approximate a non-nef target from inside the ample cone, but one ample EP class does suffice via the later necessity/sufficiency characterization; scope the perturbation limitation.
Chapter 40 rational approximation obtains bigness by openness/interiority of the big cone, not a newly proved asymptotic RR assertion here.
Do not call big-rational perturbation logically sharp when a different theorem implies an ample-class criterion.
Chapter 44 scaled approximant classes need not dominate L; distinguish convergence from a nef gap.
Constant-function closedness is a special case of varying-class decreasing closure, not the literal full statement of clause (5).

Existence of nonempty competitors for a bounded real obstacle forces nefness because a competitor is bounded below only if obstacle lower bound itself is below some competitor? Check carefully; do not infer bounded competitor from bounded obstacle.
Projection proof should use u itself as greatest competitor rather than idempotence alone.
Theorem 4.22 compares a psh function with an arbitrary usc majorant; retain this exact asymmetric form for divisorial obstacle determination.
Maximality of an obstacle envelope is stronger than least-upper-bound existence because the envelope belongs to the given competitor family.
Unbounded continuous obstacles cannot occur on compact X for finite-real codomain; unbounded-family trichotomy is for arbitrary extended obstacles.
Increasing-obstacle theorem already contains raw equality; asymmetry paragraph should not claim only a starred equality.
Supply the compactness argument with psi-epsilon and open cover for the increasing raw-envelope identity.
Conditional meets cannot be asserted without a psh lower bound; degree-one two-pole obstruction is valid and should be retained.
Necessity uses trivial semivaluations of scheme points, not a non-Archimedean GAGA theorem.
The nonunibranch example shows failure of surjectivity outside the hypotheses, not failure of the correctly stated reflection corollary.
The nodal raw-envelope operator need not attain its supremum; do not call its output a greatest psh function without EP.
Node and cusp share multiplicity/delta/embedding dimension, but other singularity invariants do distinguish them.
Cusp sections realize one specified ray slope; they do not prove descent of the whole arbitrary upstairs FS function.
Continuous cusp-envelope and exponential-envelope candidates require explicit whole-space continuity and endpoint checks before applying curve criterion.
Generalized cusp obstacle h_lambda,T must be defined explicitly, and off-ray envelope constant included.
The exponential envelope is C1 but not C2 at the transition; differentiability at the compactified infinite endpoint needs a coordinate, so scope to finite t.
Ample envelope continuity is a positive regularity result; replace blanket no-regularity statements with no-general-PL-or-C2 guarantee.
Transcendental constant alone does not obstruct PL functions with real coefficients; the nonlinear tail proves non-PL.
Classical upper-envelope fact is not uniquely a Bedford–Taylor result; avoid over-specific historical attribution.
BJ22 Remark 5.15 includes reducible X, so do not claim no extension is conjectured there.
Perfect non-algebraically-closed fields still make regularity imply smoothness; separate perfectness and residue-field hypotheses.
Later results retain their remaining hypotheses; discharging EP is not making every assertion unconditional.
Equivalences of EP reformulations are unconditional logical equivalences; later EP theorem establishes their equivalent properties.
No independent verifier or exhaustive literature claim; original whole-book edition audit reused only within recorded scope.
